title: Special characters
subtitle: Bash meta-characters — flip to reveal meaning and how they differ

cards.meaning: Comments — from # to end of line is not executed
cards.notes: Exception: #! on the first line is the sha-bang, not a comment.

cards.meaning: Command separator — two or more commands on one line, left to right
cards.example: echo one; echo two; echo three
cards.notes: Same idea as a newline. Status of the line = status of the last command. Not && (that is “and if the first succeeded”).

cards.meaning: Terminator in a case option — ends one branch
cards.example: case "$1" in start) echo starting ;; esac
cards.notes: One ; separates commands. Two ;; close a case arm. After a match, Bash leaves that option.

cards.meaning: Dot command — run a file in the current shell (same as source)
cards.notes: Space required after the dot. Variables and functions stay. Not a new process.

cards.meaning: Dot as a path component (not the source command)
cards.notes: No space: path in the current directory. Also .hidden (name starts with a dot) and .. (parent directory). Space after . → command; no space → path.

cards.meaning: Partial quoting — one word; $, backticks, and \ still work
cards.notes: Groups into one word. Variables still expand.

cards.meaning: Full quoting — one word, everything literal
cards.notes: No $ expansion, no backticks, no escape (except that ' itself cannot appear inside easily).

cards.meaning: Comma operator — links arithmetic expressions; value is the last
cards.notes: All expressions run; the value kept is the last one (here a=9, t2=5). Used in (( )) / let.

cards.meaning: Escape — next character is literal, or join lines
cards.notes: Next character loses its special meaning. If \ is last on the line, continues onto the next line.

cards.meaning: Backticks — command substitution; replaced by command output
cards.notes: Same job as $(…). Nested backticks are painful.

cards.meaning: Null command — does nothing, status 0 (like true)
cards.notes: A builtin. Placeholder, always-true condition, or no-op after a redirect. Not a semicolon.

cards.meaning: Dollar sign — starts parameter / variable expansion
cards.notes: The value of …, not the letters of the name. Also $?, $1, $(…), etc.
